requirements.requirement: Configure node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway: assign it an interface on the private network and add a source NAT/masquerade rule for that subnet out its internet-facing interface
requirements.summary: node1 eth1 was set to 10.50.50.254/24 and a persistent VyOS source NAT rule (rule 10, masquerade, source 10.50.50.0/24, outbound eth0) was committed and saved. 'show nat' confirms the rule present both before and after a full reboot, and net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 was confirmed persisted.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 are addressed on the private network so they can route through node1
requirements.summary: Persistent ifcfg-eth1 files (BOOTPROTO=static, ONBOOT=yes) were created on node2 (10.50.50.11/24) and node3 (10.50.50.12/24) and interfaces were brought up; addresses were confirmed to survive a reboot via re-read of the ifcfg files and live interface state.

requirements.requirement: Processes on node2 and node3 can actually reach the internet through node1's NAT
requirements.summary: From both node2 and node3, ping to 1.1.1.1 and curl to a public IP succeeded via a route through 10.50.50.254; on node1 the nft masquerade counters incremented and conntrack showed real source-address translation from 10.50.50.11/.12 to node1's WAN IP 10.100.245.10, directly confirming NAT was working end to end, and again after all reboots.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: For all three nodes, a pre-restart boot_id/health baseline was captured, a reboot was issued and acknowledged (VyOS: connection timeout; RHEL nodes: connection closed by remote host), a distinct post-restart boot_id was observed, and NAT config/interface addressing/connectivity were reverified as healthy afterward. This is cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle snapshots (after_executor boot_id differs from before_prepare boot_id on all three nodes) and is internally consistent with the executor's own captured boot_ids.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured node1 as a VyOS NAT gateway (eth1 = 10.50.50.254/24, persistent masquerade rule for 10.50.50.0/24 via eth0, ip_forward enabled) and statically addressed node2/node3 on the same private subnet via persistent ifcfg files. NAT functionality was directly verified end-to-end with ping, curl, nft counters, and conntrack showing real address translation from both RHEL nodes through node1. The mandatory restart protocol was executed on all three nodes with baseline/post boot_id comparison, restart acknowledgement, and reverification of NAT and connectivity after each reboot, corroborated by the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Operational hygiene is clean: the only non-final mutations were bounded, purpose-driven test routes that were fully reverted.
limitations: Native RHEL package-health checks timed out (unavailable) on node2 and node3 in both the before_prepare and after_executor snapshots, so package-state integrity for those nodes could not be independently cross-checked beyond the executor's own reports.

The lifecycle collector's after_prepare phase is an alias of before_prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the executor's own command trace rather than an independent prepare snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands are traceable to a clear purpose: NAT/interface configuration on node1, persistent interface files on node2/node3, and reboot commands for the mandatory restart protocol. The only transient mutations outside the final configuration were temporary host-route additions (1.1.1.1/32, 8.8.8.8/32 via eth1) on node2 and node3, added solely to route test traffic across the newly configured LAN interface for verification since the default route uses eth0/mgmt; these were removed within the same or a following command in every instance (cmd-4ce65aa8220e40a0, cmd-090787ce6428422c, and inline removals in cmd-5130e06d1e3c4313, cmd-b6c7450329ff4921, cmd-245bf73fe35d436a), leaving no residue. Early failed attempts (unprivileged ip addr add on node2/node3 in cmd-f24dbca343f34ea6/cmd-f409ca4f44a3479e, and a VyOS 'set system ip forwarding' typo in cmd-bcd1663f425d45ba) did not mutate state and were immediately corrected. Lifecycle diffs show no leftover files, failed services, or package-health regressions attributable to the executor beyond expected reboot-generated ephemeral systemd-private directories and /tmp/reboot.log.
